The test image shows corn plants with abnormal, proliferating bushy growth at the top — multiple small shoots and leaves growing chaotically. This strongly resembles "Crazy Top" disease caused by downy mildew.

Let me confirm with a reference image.

The reference shows early Crazy Top with leaf distortion. The test image shows the more advanced stage with proliferating multiple shoots from the growing point — the hallmark "crazy top" symptom with excessive tillering and bushy abnormal growth at the apex.

This bushy, abnormal apical proliferation is the defining symptom of Crazy Top (caused by Sclerophthora macrospora downy mildew), which replaces normal plant development with excessive tillering and leafy growth at the apex."}
